_comment: The golden set for plan 29 §7 — real routes from the production database with a
hand-checked expected outcome each, run deliberately (never in CI) before and after a
prompt change. It is checked in empty on purpose: the entries have to be verified by a
human against the live web, and inventing them would measure nothing.
Fill it with twelve to fifteen routes spanning the hard cases: a generic name, a famous
route, one with a known blog write-up, one with a published topo, and two or three that
genuinely have nothing on the web. Then run:
with Anthropic:FoundryResource configured and an az login session holding Cognitive
Services User on the Foundry resource. The run costs real money — roughly one dollar a
route (see plan 29 §5's cost note), so about $15 a pass.
expectedUrls: URLs a correct run should return. An empty array means 'nothing on the
web about this route' — a run that returns nothing for it is a success, and that rate is
the metric this plan cares most about.
